steps: Wash and finely chop the palak with the green chilli.
Knead the atta with the palak, ajwain, salt and a little water into a soft dough.
Roll into parathas and roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until spotted on both sides.
Wash and chop the methi leaves.
Mix atta, besan, methi, curd, ajwain and salt; knead into a soft dough.
Roll thin and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Rinse the poha in a strainer and let it soften.
Fry peanuts in oil, then add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli, onion and diced potato; cook until soft.
Add turmeric, salt and the poha; mix gently and steam covered for a few minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and chopped coriander.
Dry-roast the rava until fragrant and set aside.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil; add green chilli, tomato and peas and cook until soft.
Add hot water and salt, bring to a boil, then stir in the rava steadily until thick.
Soak the sabudana until soft, then drain well.
Coarsely crush the roasted peanuts.
Cook cubed potato and green chilli in oil, add sabudana, peanuts and salt, and stir until the pearls turn clear.
Cut the bread into small cubes.
Temper mustard seeds in oil; cook onion, green chilli and tomato until soft.
Add salt and the bread cubes, sprinkle a little water and toss until heated through.
Beat the eggs with salt.
Stir in finely chopped onion, tomato and coriander.
Cook on an oiled pan until set, then flip and cook the other side.
Blanch the palak in boiling water, cool, and blend to a smooth purée.
Cook onion, ginger and garlic in oil until golden; add tomato and cook down.
Add the palak purée and salt, simmer, then add paneer cubes and heat through.
Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric until soft.
Temper garlic in oil, add chopped palak and tomato and cook until wilted.
Add the cooked dal, salt and water as needed; simmer for a few minutes.
Wash and chop the methi.
Cook onion and garlic in oil until soft, then add the methi and salt.
Sprinkle besan over it and stir on low heat until dry and cooked.
Boil the tomatoes until soft, then blend and strain.
Temper curry leaves in oil or ghee, add the tomato juice, jaggery, salt and water.
Simmer briefly and finish with chopped coriander.
Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric and mash until smooth; add salt and water to a pouring consistency.
Cook the rice.
Serve hot varan over rice with a spoon of ghee and a squeeze of lemon.
Rinse and soak the rice.
Cook brinjal pieces and peas in oil with goda masala and salt.
Add the rice and water, cover and cook until done; top with coriander.
Make a stuffing of crushed roasted peanuts, onion, goda masala, coriander and salt.
Slit the small brinjals and fill them with the stuffing.
Cook covered in oil with a little water, turning gently, until the brinjals are soft.
Roast the brinjal directly on the flame until the skin chars and the inside is soft.
Peel and mash the flesh.
Mix with chopped onion, green chilli, curd and salt.
Knead jowar flour with warm water; pat into bhakris and roast on a tawa.
For pithla, cook onion and green chilli in oil, add water and salt, then whisk in besan.
Stir until thick and garnish with coriander; serve with the bhakri.
Mix jowar and bajra flour, besan, chopped onion, coriander, ajwain and salt with water into a dough.
Pat thin rounds onto a greased tawa and make a few holes in each.
Roast with a little oil until crisp on both sides.
Use sprouted matki (soak, drain and keep covered until sprouted).
Cook onion and tomato in oil with goda masala.
Add the sprouts, salt and water; cook until tender and top with coriander.
Finely chop the cucumber and tomato.
Add crushed roasted peanuts, curd and salt.
Mix and top with chopped coriander; serve fresh.
Cut the cauliflower into florets and the potato into cubes.
Cook onion in oil until soft, then add tomato, turmeric and salt.
Add the vegetables, cover and cook until tender.
Grate the cauliflower and mix with coriander, ajwain and salt.
Knead the atta into a soft dough; stuff each ball with the filling.
Roll gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Wash and dry the bhindi completely, then slice.
Cook in oil with onion until no longer sticky.
Sprinkle besan and salt and stir until crisp.
Shred the cabbage finely.
Temper mustard seeds in oil, add green chilli, turmeric and peas.
Add the cabbage and salt; cook uncovered until just tender.
Soak the chana dal, then cook it until just soft.
Cook peeled, cubed dudhi with tomato in oil with turmeric and salt.
Add the chana dal and a little water; simmer until the dudhi is soft.
Whisk curd, besan and water until smooth.
Temper curry leaves and ginger in oil, then add the curd mixture and salt.
Simmer on low heat, stirring, until it thickens.
Crumble the paneer.
Cook onion, capsicum and tomato in oil until soft.
Add the paneer, turmeric and salt; stir until heated through.
Rinse and soak the rice.
Cook the carrot, peas, capsicum and potato briefly in oil.
Add the rice, salt and water; cover and cook until the rice is done.
Rinse the rice and cook it in the milk on low heat, stirring often.
When the rice is soft and the milk has thickened, add sugar.
Simmer a few more minutes; serve warm or chilled.
Wash and cut the fruit just before eating.
Mix banana, papaya and apple in a bowl.
Serve straight away; cut fruit doesn't keep long.
Cook chopped onion and capsicum in oil.
Sprinkle besan and salt and mix well.
Stir on low heat, adding a little water, until dry and crumbly.
Cook the rice and let it cool slightly.
Fry peanuts and curry leaves in oil with mustard seeds and turmeric.
Toss in the rice with salt and lemon juice.
Chop the palak and onion.
Mix with besan, salt and just enough water to coat.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry until crisp.
Grate the carrots.
Cook them in ghee, then add milk and simmer, stirring, until the milk is absorbed.
Add sugar and cook until glossy.
Roast the rava in ghee until fragrant.
Add hot milk and stir until thick.
Mix in sugar and mashed banana; cook for a minute more.
